member.name: JingleFirstScan
member.para: The recorded proof that the skipped pause windows buy nothing. Build 331 of "Die Cyber-Brutzellen": the seven chapters build 339 accepted "at a silence" were accepted "at a jingle" by build 331 at the same millisecond, and the 1256 extra probes between the two runs bought no mark at all.

Experimental (0.12.1). The corpus evidence for the shape is strong on the books it targets and there is none at all for the books it does not, which is what --jingle-first is for - it forces the shape on so a book outside the gate can be measured without rebuilding the tool.

Why leaving the head open at the top costs nothing (2026-08-20, measured over the build-362 corpus run before the change shipped). The concern was that an open head could accept a second copy of the very chapter that closes it, from a window reaching over the boundary onto its announcement - which would have moved chapter 1 on every jingle book rather than fixing a rare one. Two independent measurements say it cannot:

First, the bound had never rejected anything. IsOutOfSequence logs every number it turns down at an upper bound, and across all seventeen books that line appears exactly twice - "at or above 32" and "at or above 8", both sequence-gap re-probes. Not once at a head stretch's bound of 1, so no head window has ever produced a numbered phrase match at all and removing the bound admits nothing that was not admitted already.

Second, the geometry forbids it: RegionProber.WindowEndFor clamps a window to _region.ToSeconds, and a head stretch ends at the closing chapter's mark, which sits one --mark-lead ahead of the announcement's first word. The margins are far wider than that in practice - BARDIOC's last head window ends about 4 s short of the boundary and Stalker's about 2 min 45 s short. Note this rests on the region clamp in window planning, which is why JingleFirst_TheHeadStretchCannotReAcceptTheChapterThatClosesIt pins it.

What the heads do hold is the shape that produced build 328's phantom chapters - Perry Rhodan Zeittafel year lists read as bare numbers at segment starts, "3585. Die Invasionsflotte der Lahren ..." at 0:07:29 of BARDIOC, "2040 bis 2329. Das Solare Imperium entsteht ..." at 0:01:10 of Stalker. Two independent things stop those becoming chapters: under a phrase run they would have to be spoken as "Kapitel N", and they are above --max-chapter-number's default of 200 either way. The second is load-bearing, so this change and that cap should not be reconsidered independently of one another.

Confirmed inert on real audio (build 365 against the build-350 reference, same machine, the 30-minute ddm-jf.m4b head clip of "Die Dritte Macht"): both marks identical - 0:03:07.24 at confidence 0.57 / -65.8 dBFS and 0:23:43.05 at 0.61 / -73.7 dBFS, every digit the same - on 14 probes against 14, with the head stretch now reading "open at the top" where it read "below chapter 1" and no upper-bound rejection logged anywhere. So the openness costs neither a mark nor a probe on the shape it changes.

Not exercised by any corpus book. The condition fires on all nine jingle-first books (every one of them has the jingle half find chapter 1 first), but the defect it fixes needs a file whose head holds a previous part's chapters - a multi-part book whose earlier parts carry no music. None is on hand, so what is measured here is that the change is inert, not that it works. Two further reads of the bound flip with it and are equally unexercised: RegionProber.RestartTrackingAllowed switches on for the head, which is the half that would actually recognise a previous part, and WideBareNumberReading switches off, leaving the head with the narrow reading and no isolation guard - the same pairing a forward scan already gets, and reachable only by a bare-number book with jingles.
